reviewNote: Reviewed the five approved multiprocess repairs: per-execution fresh nonce admission uses atomic SQLite compare/update and kernel-owned per-run OS lock liveness (no heartbeat/env flags); startup skips live peer writers. Node ALS scopes session/WAL/task/inbox/approval writes across awaited host callbacks, including empty-claim revocation; explicit generation writes are always fenced. Both kernels await complete outcome handling before releasing, including handleTurnCompletion.then, guard stale catch/cleanup and retain compatible optional host ports for mini without Node imports. Approval decision/continuation/state are one transaction and revoke a parked claim only after persisting its authorized control message. Cancellation handles the saved-last-decision window, fences old callback tokens, and daemon continuation uses the actual current checkpoint. Tool dispatch checks abort/current generation between chunks and immediately before execution. SDK skills synchronized. Legacy writer test now requires legitimate release and still asserts stale-write rejection; legacy cancellation test strengthens running to failed/aborted while retaining parked cleanup. Observation cuts remain before admission/release reads and before the atomic approval transaction; no state reconstruction. Source mutants updated to disable actual new live-writer guard/CAS release, still requiring new red cases from green baselines. Final review: admission failure preserves an existing controller; the runtime owns cleanup of the controller it created. New SDK regression first failed and is part of the full suite. Historical prepared snapshots remain append-only observations and are not blocked after ordinary run completion. Fresh-input and late-approval controls, stale rejection trace, live-peer boot and dead-peer handoff extend coverage to 62 OS-process scenarios without changing Given/When/Then. Late stream regression explicitly uses runTurnStream, first reproduced old chunks reaching direct/follower consumers, then passed after the same ALS generation fence was applied at delivery. No stream is published from a revoked generation; normal approval follower tests remain green. Final metadata/docs review after all-green probes: verification and five-fix specs promoted to implemented with exact criteria equality checked. Only status and explanatory skill/documentation changed after validation; original counterexample evidence remains intact. Review follow-up after integration of origin/main factory delivery/development: reviewed pre-admission abort isolation, live Bot/subagent ownership during recovery handoff, and transactional unattended-approval expiry outside the inherited turn scope with matching-pause validation. Real timer regressions verify expiry cleanup and restoration of stale-writer rejection. Reviewed context persistence through SQLite/in-memory inbox, edit/claim/drain/subagent routes and additive v31 migration; lossy overflow retains bounded fenced attachment excerpts with delimiter neutralization. SDK guides updated. These added mapping paths are source-review dependencies, not claims that bounded process fixtures exercise every UI or expiry path. Acceptance criteria were not weakened; original counterexample evidence retained. Legacy checkpointless parked hosts retain expiry settlement only with no writer and no pending approvals; checkpointed sessions still require matching pause IDs. Existing delegated Bot expiry and all expiry regressions pass (47 targeted tests). CI-only review: tests job timeout increased from 20 to 35 minutes after measured formal regression took 314 seconds; all verification steps, evidence uploads, child timeouts and failure gates remain intact. Reviewed kernel admission refactor: public runSessionKernel is an unchanged-signature alias to a small admission/scope wrapper; the established top-level turn implementation and helper identities are preserved. Claim, checkpoint reread, asynchronous completion, stale rejection and finally release retain their ordering and writer scope. SDK test explicitly checks model/completion/release scope and public cleanup. No CRAP baseline or threshold change. PR #189 post-merge vertical review: confirmed and repaired the read/admission checkpoint race in both kernels. After claiming, writer scope re-reads session, agent and pending approvals; a new pending checkpoint is preserved, a consumed pause does not restart the model, a newly approved wave uses only its latest tool IDs, and waiting-event failures release the claim. Independent runtime regression exercises both kernels at a deterministic claim boundary (10 cases), alongside existing actual-process gates; this is not a proof over arbitrary schedules. Existing criteria and mutation/check thresholds are unchanged.
